name: Grand piano (Kawai)
note: An instrument recipe for the sampler (doc 24, Instruments, Sample preparation and Sampler rules). It describes exactly the files the prep step produced; nothing here is a tuning choice. type, id, name, version: what this is. source: where the recordings come from (library, folder url, license) and what the library's own note files say (notes). channels: channel count of every file. formats: each file exists once per format under root, as <file>.ogg (Ogg Opus, 48 kHz, 96 kbps stereo or 64 kbps mono, variable bitrate) and <file>.m4a (AAC-LC at the source rate, 128 kbps stereo or 96 kbps mono); the browser picks the first it can play. root: folder of the files, relative to the repo. layers: the number of velocity layers in the sustain set, layer 1 the quietest. sets: one entry per articulation: sus (sustain, pedal down or natural ring), nosus (dampers working), rel (release or key-off noise, played on note-off), pedal (sounds of the pedal mechanism). Each set has source (the library subfolder) and zones; a zone is one recorded key: note (scientific pitch, C4 = middle C, sharps written s in file names), midi (C4 = 60). measuredCents: the zone's measured pitch offset from 12-tone equal temperament at A4 = 440 Hz, in cents, as recorded; piano strings are inharmonic (partial n sits at n f0 sqrt(1 + B n^2)), so it is fitted from partials 1 to 6 (2 to 8 in the bass, where the fundamental is weak) over a window of the early sustain, each partial taken as the level-weighted centre of its unison-string cluster, and it is the pitch of the fitted first partial. Real pianos are stretch-tuned on purpose (bass flat, treble sharp); nothing has been corrected. tuneLayer: the layer the zone's number comes from (the middle one). tuneResidualCents: how far the found partials sit from the fit (root mean square, cents). tunePartials: which partials were found and used. layerSpreadCents: the largest difference between this zone's layers. inharmonicityB: the fitted B. unisonSplitCents: the widest spread seen inside one partial's cluster (a sign of unison strings tuned apart, which is heard as beating or chorus). tuneConfidence: 0 to 1, falls with fewer partials, a larger residual and a larger layer spread; below about 0.5 trust the ear over the number. layers: the files of the zone, quietest first; file is the path under root without extension; layer is its velocity layer and rr its round-robin take when the set has takes. peakDb: the file's sample peak in dBFS. attackRmsDb: the RMS level of its first 300 ms after the onset, in dBFS. Whether these levels mean anything depends on the source (see levels below). brightness: the share of energy above 1.5 times the note's fundamental (or 1 kHz, whichever is higher) in those first 300 ms, which should rise from layer to layer; in a very quiet file the noise floor can inflate it. lenS: length after the prep, in seconds. trimStartMs: how much was cut from the start (the onset, the first point above -50 dB of the file's peak, is kept with 3 ms before it). measuredCents on a layer is that file's own measurement. src: the original file name. Every file was cut where its 50 ms RMS fell to 60 dB below its peak, or at a maximum length (8 s at A0 falling evenly per semitone to 4 s at C8 for sustains, 2 s for releases), whichever came first, then given an equal-power fade over its last 250 ms (100 ms for releases and pedal sounds) so it ends in true silence. No gain was changed. levels: whether the source normalised each file (normalized true: the levels say nothing about how hard the key was played, so the sampler rebuilds the dynamic range from velocity with its own curve and must not re-gain the layers) or kept the recorded levels (normalized false: the layers already step up in level as they were played, and the sampler should play them at their own level). range: the lowest and highest sustain zone. problems: anything odd found while preparing, in plain words. The .m4a files decode about 23 ms longer than the .ogg files because AAC pads its last frame with silence; the start is in the same place in both. Kawai: the source names are an octave low (A#-1 for A#0); the names here are corrected and src keeps the original.

source.notes: Folder 'Grand Piano, Kawai' (not the older 'Grand Piano, Kawai - Legacy' folder, which is a different, earlier cut). Files GPiano_sus_* and GPiano_rel_*, mic 'Player' (player's position). Subfolders Sustains and Releases. Velocity layers v1 to v4 in the source, kept as v1 to v4. One round robin. Legacy.txt in this folder contains only the word 'LEGACY!'; it carries no instruction we could act on, and since this is the folder the brief asked for we used it as is (the separate Legacy folder's own note, 'Normal is Normalized.txt', says its files are normalised, to use a velocity curve for dynamics, and apologises for 'funky tuning'). The note names in these files are one octave low against scientific pitch: the file named A#-1 sounds A#0 (58.3 Hz), C3 sounds C4, and so on, which pitch measurement confirmed on every zone; every file here is named and placed one octave up from its source name (the original name is kept in src).

levels.note: Recorded levels kept: across the set v1 peaks sit near -40 to -54 dBFS and v4 near -5 to -13 dBFS, so the layers carry the real dynamic range. Play them at their own level (a gentle overall make-up gain is fine; do not level the layers against each other).

problems: The Kawai's lowest files, named A#-1 (A#0 after the octave fix), sound A0 about 11 to 14 cents flat (partials every 27.4 Hz), so they are placed at A0. The key's release files, also named A#-1, are placed with them at A0.

8 sustain files end in the source before falling to -60 dB or reaching the maximum length, so the 250 ms fade lands on a still-audible tail (tail level when the file ends: -53.3 to -37.4 dB below peak): sus/A6-v1 (2.389 s), sus/A7-v1 (1.396 s), sus/C7-v1 (2.991 s), sus/C8-v1 (1.064 s), sus/Ds6-v1 (3.316 s), sus/Ds7-v1 (1.621 s), sus/Fs6-v1 (3.404 s), sus/G7-v1 (1.902 s)

sus/Ds2-v1 (GPiano_sus_D#1_v1_rr1_Player.wav): pitch check flagged it; reviewed by hand: partials sit at 77.1, 154.7, 231.8, 309.6 Hz, so this is D#2 as placed; the automatic octave flag came from low rumble peaks in a very quiet layer (peak -41 dB)

sus/Fs5-v1 (GPiano_sus_F#4_v1_rr1_Player.wav): pitch check flagged it; reviewed by hand: the soft layer is almost a pure fundamental at 739 Hz (F#5) with weak upper partials, which tripped the automatic check; the note is right
sus/Fs6-v2 (GPiano_sus_F#5_v2_rr1_Player.wav): pitch check flagged it; reviewed by hand: fundamental at 1479 Hz (F#6), weak upper partials; the note is right
sus/A0-v2 (GPiano_sus_A#-1_v2_rr1_Player.wav): placed at A0, not As0 as its name says, because it measurably sounds A0 (-13.92 cents)
sus/A0-v3 (GPiano_sus_A#-1_v3_rr1_Player.wav): placed at A0, not As0 as its name says, because it measurably sounds A0 (-14.01 cents)
sus/A0-v4 (GPiano_sus_A#-1_v4_rr1_Player.wav): placed at A0, not As0 as its name says, because it measurably sounds A0 (-10.67 cents)
rel/A0-v2 (GPiano_rel_A#-1_v2_rr1_Player.wav): placed at A0, not As0 as its name says, because it is the release of that key
rel/A0-v3 (GPiano_rel_A#-1_v3_rr1_Player.wav): placed at A0, not As0 as its name says, because it is the release of that key
rel/A0-v4 (GPiano_rel_A#-1_v4_rr1_Player.wav): placed at A0, not As0 as its name says, because it is the release of that key

onset check: in 47 encoded files the -30 dB threshold crossing moved by more than 2 ms after encoding (codec ripple on a slow, quiet attack); cross-correlation of the first 80 ms against the processed WAV shows no shift in any of them (lag 0 to 0.02 ms), so the starts are in place

sus zones further apart than a whole tone (doc 24 sampler rule: at most 2 semitones): A0 to C1 (3 semitones), C1 to Ds1 (3 semitones), Ds1 to Fs1 (3 semitones), Fs1 to A1 (3 semitones), A1 to C2 (3 semitones), C2 to Ds2 (3 semitones), Ds2 to Fs2 (3 semitones), Fs2 to A2 (3 semitones), A2 to C3 (3 semitones), C6 to Ds6 (3 semitones), Ds6 to Fs6 (3 semitones), Fs6 to A6 (3 semitones), A6 to C7 (3 semitones), C7 to Ds7 (3 semitones), Ds7 to Fs7 (3 semitones), A7 to C8 (3 semitones)
